prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B016 as a single prize part for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific case is the chain from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide, through human incretin physiology and receptor biology, to drugs with randomized cardiovascular, renal and weight outcome evidence. It is original, independently confirmed, mature and clinically very large, and no member has raised a maturity concern. The chair's observation is right that the real remaining question is attribution, and I decide it on the discovery criterion. The prize in this category rewards the discovery that opens a field. Identification of the active truncated peptide and its physiology is the step on which every later analogue depends, so the citation is best anchored in that step and is easiest to trace in the primary literature. A one-part prize is also the cleanest reading of the evidence; I do not see a case that requires a second part this year.
statement.case_against: The weak point is Mojsov. Her priority for identifying and synthesising the active form is contested by the Habener group, who are not credited here, and the supplied record does not let me settle it. If the committee cannot defend her inclusion against that claim, the citation is exposed. The trio also omits Knudsen, whose acylated long-acting analogues made the biology a medicine, so a reader could say the prize honours the idea and not the drug. I have therefore tested my own position against the Knudsen configuration. I still hold that the physiology trio is more defensible, but I accept it is a close judgement, and if the committee concludes the Mojsov priority is unresolved I would move to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen rather than keep a contested name.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that carrying the physiology through to the therapy favours Knudsen, because acylated long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide) are what made the biology matter to patients, and that a basic trio is defensible but not clearly right.
responses.response: I agree that Knudsen's engineering is the step that produced the drugs, and that a prize without her can read as neglecting the medicine. My disagreement is about what the criterion rewards. Her work depends on an established mechanism and on the active peptide, and the Nobel category has usually credited the discovery with the drug as proof of its importance. I also note your fallback is the same as mine in reverse: we both accept the other trio as defensible. The question I would put to you is whether you can defend omitting the person who identified the active form if Mojsov's record holds up. If it does not hold up, I think we converge on Drucker, Holst and Knudsen.

responses.point: Linnarsson includes Knudsen so that the prize stays faithful to the complete arc from physiology to a once-weekly drug, and acknowledges that the basic-discovery trio is cleaner and less exposed to criticism.
responses.response: Your concession that the basic trio is cleaner and less exposed is the point I find most persuasive for my own choice. I accept the arc-to-medicine argument, and your citation wording is attractive. But your uncertainty about the priority history rests on recollection that you say is unverified, and I share that limit. Since neither of us can resolve it from the record, I would not let an unverified recollection decide the third name either way. I weigh a citation naming the active peptide as the better-supported wording, but I would sign the Knudsen version if the committee judges the priority record unclear.

responses.point: Sandberg backs Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, says Mojsov's priority against Habener is genuinely contested, and suggests that if the dispute cannot be resolved a different configuration, or a different year, may be more defensible.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of your position, and I share your discomfort over forcing a contested name. I would not follow you to deferring the topic to another year. The science is mature and recognition is already late, and the dispute concerns a single name, not the discovery. If the dispute is unresolved, the committee has a clear fallback in Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, which keeps the prize this year without crediting a disputed priority claim. I would therefore put the Knudsen swap ahead of postponement.

responses.point: The chair holds the basic-discovery trio, notes that Mojsov's priority is contested and that Knudsen would be the safer configuration, and asks whether a second prize part such as B007 or B008 should be added.
responses.response: On the second part, I do not support adding one. The reduction to one or two GLP-1 names would require dropping Holst, Drucker or Mojsov, and every cut is harder to defend than the omission of Knudsen. CAR-T also carries unresolved credit among Rosenberg, June, Sadelain and the uncredited Eshhar, so a two-name B007 would add an attribution dispute to a prize that already has one. I would keep B016 alone. I agree with you that this is a close judgement on the third name, and I would accept your safer configuration if the committee finds the Mojsov record unresolved.

responses.point: El Manira holds Drucker, Holst and Mojsov on the grounds that the prize rewards the discovery of a physiological mechanism, with therapy as the proof of importance, and treats optogenetics as strong but hard to attribute under a three-name limit.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of what the category rewards, and with your view that either choice of third laureate can be criticised. On optogenetics, I was also uneasy about cutting six names to three, and your own difficulty choosing among Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann supports that. It is a strong candidate for a later year. It does not need to be resolved now because B016 already gives a coherent single prize.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1 peptide can be defended against the Habener group on the supplied record. This is the main reason I might move to Knudsen.
Whether the committee will frame the prize around the physiology and active peptide or around the full arc to long-acting analogues, since this decides the third laureate.
Whether CAR-T (B007) can be credited cleanly without Rosenberg and Eshhar, and whether cGAS-STING (B005) is clinically mature enough, which matter only if a second part is considered.
Whether my ranking of the basic-discovery trio reflects the criterion or a bias toward mechanism, since the Knudsen configuration is equally defensible.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict applies to B016. I work on autoimmunity and type I interferon biology, which is topically adjacent to cGAS-STING (B005) and to CAR-T use in autoimmune disease (B007), two of my alternatives. This is topical overlap with no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited name, and it does not change my position from round 1.
